stress.detail: 5 MB response relayed, recorded, and replayed intact (0.11s through the proxy)
2,000 sequential calls, all recorded (0.41 ms per round trip incl. client)
5 recordings started at the same instant on a new database, 200 calls each, nothing lost
server died mid-call: agent sees end-of-stream, relayorb exits with the server's code (3), session saved with the unanswered call
SIGTERM to relayorb: server stopped, session saved (relayorb exit 1)
relayorb killed with SIGKILL: server exits on its own (stdin closes), calls recorded so far are kept; session stays marked running
non-JSON line on stdout: forwarded untouched, recorded and shown as (not JSON-RPC), session continues
JSON-RPC batch: both calls recorded and paired; replay answers a batch with a batch
unicode, emoji, line/paragraph separators, escapes: byte-exact through the proxy and in the recording
2,000 progress notifications during one call: all forwarded in order and recorded

agents.setup: relayorb binary as the MCP command, filesystem server
two runs, file changed in between, `relayorb diff` pinpoints the changed call

fixed: `record`: if relayorb was killed (SIGKILL) right after a call, that call could be missing from the recording. Messages are now stored before they are forwarded.
`check`: tools that ask the agent something mid-call (LLM sampling) failed, because check answered with an error. It now answers the way the agent did in the recording.
Windows: `relayorb record -- npx ...` could not start the server (`npx` is a `.cmd` file). Commands are now resolved like `cmd.exe` does. This affected 0.3.0 on Windows.
Windows: when several recordings started at the same instant on a new database, one could exit with "database is locked". Database setup now retries.
not_tested: Agents other than Claude Code: Cursor, Codex, Claude Desktop, VS Code. They use the same stdio protocol, but nobody has run them yet.
Remote MCP servers over HTTP. RelayOrb does not support them yet.
The Intel macOS and Linux ARM binaries. They are built and published but were not run in this suite.
Alpine Linux (musl). The Linux binaries need glibc.
Very long-running sessions (hours) and recordings databases larger than a few hundred MB.
